name: Research and Evidence
summary: Research findings, monitoring and evaluation data, and evidence base for agri-energy interventions in Uganda — supporting adaptive programming and investment decisions.
description: The agri-energy sector in Uganda is growing, but there is still a limited evidence base on technology performance, socioeconomic impacts, gender outcomes, and cost-benefit profiles from Ugandan field conditions. This thematic area curates research papers, programme evaluations, case documentation, and dataset publications that improve the evidence base for agri-energy decision-making. Topics include technology performance monitoring, gender impact assessments, market assessments for renewable energy equipment, smallholder willingness-to-pay studies, and comparative analyses of business models. A stronger evidence base helps donors, government, and implementing partners design more effective programmes and allocate resources to the most impactful interventions.
whyItMatters: Without robust Ugandan evidence, agri-energy programmes risk repeating mistakes, over-promising results, and failing to learn from what has already been tried. Research and evidence generation is a public good that benefits the entire sector. Curating and sharing this evidence through the Agri-Energy Desk helps ensure that lessons are not lost and that the sector builds learning progressively.
